shared_elements: horizontal band or register divider running across the surface
repeated small rounded/hatched surface texture (curls in A, arch row and strokes in B)
justification: Both are shallow stone reliefs organised with profile subjects arranged along horizontal registers, and both use a repeated small-unit texture as a band (the tiered curls and beard rows in A, the arcade of arch shapes and stroke fringe in B). The decisive difference is subject and handling: A shows two large, richly modelled bearded human heads confronting each other with careful volumetric detail, while B is a flat, schematic array of small animal and abstract signs distributed over a tall pillar, so neither the compositional scheme nor the carving manner really corresponds.
